mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained unemployment rate increases above 0.3pp.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and accelerating inflation, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both HOUST and GDPC1 on a month-over-month basis indicates strengthening housing demand and overall economic activity, which boosts corporate revenues and profit expectations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both HOUST and GDPC1 rise month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in PAYEMS above 0.5% for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during five consecutive months of PAYEMS growth above 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in RSAFS below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals weakening retail sales momentum, which reduces consumer spending and corporate revenue, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12mo MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months.
